prompts: We need a landing page, {WS}/landing/index.html in a single file, for the story of Piet Mondrian's "Composition with Red, Blue and Yellow" (1930). The facts are in {WS}/FACTSHEET.md, and nothing beyond them should be claimed. A visitor should leave knowing the painter, the year, the movement and why the work matters, and be invited to read more at the source the fact sheet gives. The page itself should speak Mondrian's visual language. It is reviewed by opening the file, with no build step, in a browser that reaches only Google Fonts and https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/build/three.module.js.
answers:
[action] Wrote `landing/index.html` (single file, no build), then verified it live in the browser over three passes.

**Approach and assumptions**
- Hero: the painting rebuilt in pure CSS grid (red square top right, blue bottom left, yellow rectangle bottom right, thick black gaps on white) so the core visual works even without JS; a decorative three.js stage extrudes the same blocks and slowly rotates, wrapped in try/catch so a CDN failure leaves the page unchanged.
- External requests limited to Google Fonts (Archivo + Space Grotesk) and the exact three@0.170.0 module URL. No images, no other CDNs.
- Copy is strictly the fact sheet: painter/dates, 1930, oil on canvas, Kunsthaus Zurich, De Stijl (founded 1917, van Doesburg + Mondrian), Neoplasticism principles, the picture description, why it matters, plus the alternate title. The CTA links to the Wikipedia source URL from the sheet.
- Reduced-motion respected; composition grid has an aria-label; focus-visible outlines; semantic sections.

[result] Evidence from opening the file in the browser:
- Screenshots confirm the hero CSS composition matches the described layout, and the movement/cards/CTA/footer sections render with Google Fonts (`document.fonts.check` → `true`).
- three.js loaded from the jsdelivr URL: `#three-holder canvas` present; after fixing my block coordinates, the 3D render shows white top-left, red top-right, blue bottom-left, white middle, yellow bottom-right on black, matching the painting.
- CTA href read back byte-exact: `https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Composition_with_Red,_Blue_and_Yellow`.
- Last edit pulls the camera to z=17.5 so the rotating square isn't clipped in the 16:9 stage (geometry: visible height ≈ 12.4 units vs. a 10.4-unit frame).

[next] Nothing pending; the 2 allowed revision rounds are used (geometry fix, camera framing).
checks: has a page title and an h1
names the painting (Composition with Red, Blue and Yellow)
links to the fact sheet's source
CSS with the Mondrian palette (red, blue, yellow, black)
